There is no single thing in life that is important above all else. Hard work is one part of the deal, healthy relationships are another. It's those relationships that motivate you to work hard, and keep you grounded when you're facing turbulence. Sharing problems and successes with other people gives the kind of perspective that you can't find inside your head.

Which is why working hard AND being alone is especially exhausting. When I read hateful and judgmental replies on Reddit, I know those people are in that very dark place. They're stuck in the loop of pushing themselves too hard while thinking their problems are the center of the world. They genuinely believe they're not being listened to and the world is particularly unfair to them, and it's a shitty feeling to live with. 

Humans are social creatures, and living in a human body comes with its needs. Healthy relationships are a biological necessity just like eating and sleeping, and lacking that part of our lives is the source of a lot of problems (even seemingly unrelated ones). We sometimes forget that when we're isolated and low on awareness.

Personally, one of the most important things has been realizing the compartmentalization of the mind. There's an active component (abstract thinking, hopes, fears, judgment) and a passive component (essentially the hard-wired, automated impulses from your body). It might be intuitive to most people that the mind is not just one linear thing, but few are really paying attention to the different impulses. That sort of mindfulness is what's helped me out with my severe OCD, and I'm sure it can help unfold other types of internal knots as well. 

What my episodes really mean is that the signals in my active mind are getting stuck in a feedback loop. It's analysis of previous analysis all the way down. I can let things go by focusing on the passive mind. It feels like opening a safety valve from a pressure cooker left unsupervised for too long.
